A file that keeps growing ends up doing many unrelated things, and finding anything in it means scrolling. This rule reports a file that has more lines than the maximum, which is 300 by default.

## Examples

With a maximum of 4, this file of 5 lines is reported:

{/* bad {"options": [4]} */}
```js
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const text = await readFile("notes.txt", "utf8");

console.log(text.split("\n").length);
```

Not reported, with the work moved to another file:

{/* good {"options": [4]} */}
```js
import { countLines } from "./count-lines.js";
console.log(await countLines("notes.txt"));
```

## Options

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
max-lines = ["error", { max = 500, skipBlankLines = true, skipComments = true }]
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max` | `300` | The number of lines a file can have. |
| `skipBlankLines` | `false` | Do not count lines that are empty or only have whitespace. |
| `skipComments` | `false` | Do not count lines that only have a comment. A line with code and a comment still counts. |

A number alone is short for `{ "max": number }`.

With `skipBlankLines`, the first example has 3 lines:

{/* good {"options": [{"max": 4, "skipBlankLines": true}]} */}
```js
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const text = await readFile("notes.txt", "utf8");

console.log(text.split("\n").length);
```

With `skipComments`, so does this one:

{/* good {"options": [{"max": 4, "skipComments": true}]} */}
```js
// Prints the number of lines in notes.txt.
// Run it with: bun count.js
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
const text = await readFile("notes.txt", "utf8");
console.log(text.split("\n").length);
```

## When not to use it

Generated files, fixtures and long tables of data are long for a good reason. Turn the rule off for them.
